# Jane Andrews

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c28 P0](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0000), [v1 c28 P11](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0011)</sub>
- **Origin:** Avonlea  <sub>[v1 c33 P47](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0047)</sub>
- **Role:** Student  <sub>[v1 c28 P9](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0009)</sub>

## Appearance

Jane is a schoolgirl who participates in play-acting alongside her friends. During these games, she was assigned the role of Guinevere while wearing dramatic attire for their group's outdoor play.

_Sources: [v1 c28 P7](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0007), [v1 c28 P11](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0011)_

## Personality

Jane is practical, cautious, and outspokenly realistic, often balancing out the more imaginative ideas of her peers. She admits to being easily distracted during dramatic games and finds comfort in material wealth, believing that luxury and diamonds can provide genuine solace.

_Sources: [v1 c28 P2](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0002), [v1 c33 P47](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0047)_

## Traits

- Cautious  <sub>[v1 c28 P2](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0002)</sub>
- Pragmatic  <sub>[v1 c28 P2](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0002), [v1 c33 P47](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0047)</sub>
- Materialistic  <sub>[v1 c33 P47](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0047)</sub>

## Abilities

- Acting  <sub>[v1 c28 P11](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0011)</sub>

## History

Jane spent a midsummer afternoon playing with Diana Barry, Ruby Gillis, and Anne Shirley by the pond below Orchard Slope. The girls studied Tennyson's poem in school and decided to dramatize the story of Elaine, with Jane taking on the role of Guinevere as well as one of the brothers and the father. During their play, Jane expressed practical reservations about lying motionless in a floating boat, stating she would constantly pop up to check where she was drifting. In a later conversation with Anne, Jane admitted her perspective on wealth, maintaining that diamonds could comfort a person through many difficulties.

_Sources: [v1 c28 P2](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0002), [v1 c28 P7](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0007), [v1 c28 P9](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0009), [v1 c28 P11](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0011), [v1 c33 P47](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0047)_

## Quotes

> Of course it would be romantic, but I know I couldn’t keep still. I’d be popping up every minute or so to see where I was and if I wasn’t drifting too far out. And you know, Anne, that would spoil the effect.  <sub>[v1 c28 P2](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0002)</sub>

> I don’t know—exactly. I think diamonds would comfort a person for a good deal.  <sub>[v1 c33 P47](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0047)</sub>
